sources.citation: Grambank language page libi1244 (coder Hedvig Skirgård), sole source van Leynseele 1977.
sources.note: Grambank has no stress feature; confirms van Leynseele 1977 was the source the coders had.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1950. Eigenaardige toonstructuur van enkele Bantoetalen in het noord-westen van Belgisch-Kongo. Kongo-Overzee 16(1): 37-53; De tonologie der naamwoorden van Eniele en Bokonzi. 16(2-3): 112-124; De tonologie der naamwoorden te Ebuku. 16(5): 281-291.
sources.note: Noun tonology of Bomboma-sector villages (Botoko, Likpangbala, Eniele, Bokonzi, Maleke-Moleke, Moliba, Ebuku -- Bomboma C411 area, 'sector en gewest Bomboma'), not Libinza. No stress remarks.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2009. Le réseau fluvial congolais et la problématique de l'expansion bantoue. Annales Aequatoria 30: 839-988.
sources.note: Libinza examples only at p. 909 (locative-infinitive, from 'Van Leynseele, 1976/1977: A1') and p. 950 (negation by tone); section 3.2.2 Tonologie is comparative; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu. 1990. Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre: éléments de structure grammaticale. (Études Aequatoria 8.) Bamanya-Mbandaka: Centre Aequatoria. 284 pp.
sources.note: Has a 'Sous-groupe Libinza' (pp. 222-273) but only sketches Litoka/Ewaku, Balobo and Ndobo -- no Libinza-proper sketch; each sketch's phonology covers vowels, consonants, tone ('La tonologie, quant à elle, est du type lingala', Litoka, p. 223); the word 'accent' never occurs; silent on Libinza stress. Intro p. 4 (p. 7) states the only Libinza description is 'l'étude de H. Van Leynseele (16) sur le Libinza.. dont le manuscrit est disponible au Centre Aequatoria de Bamanya'.

sources.citation: [Kadima Kamuleta?] 1988. Article on class-5 nominal prefixes in Zairean languages (quotes Sere 1985 Libinza data). Annales Aequatoria 9: c. 120-121 (+ notes 21-22 p. 130).
sources.note: Morphology only (li-/zV- alternation in Libinza nouns from Sere 1985: 30); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1951. La tonologie des parlers bantous du nord-ouest du Congo belge. Bulletin des Séances, Institut Royal Colonial Belge 22(4): 900-919.
sources.note: Regional tonology survey: the 'Bangala-des-grandes-eaux' (riverains of the Ubangi, Congo, Ngiri, Mongala..) have the 'type lingala' tonology (pp. 903-904). Libinza not named; nothing on stress or accent.
sources.venue: Bulletin des Séances, Institut Royal Colonial Belge

sources.citation: Donzo Bunza Yugia, Jean-Pierre. 2015. Langues bantoues de l'entre Congo-Ubangi (RD Congo): documentation, reconstruction, classification et contacts avec les langues oubanguiennes [thesis report]. Afrika Focus 28(1): 109-119.

tone.summary: Short thesis report on ten Congo-Ubangi Bantu languages (bonyange among them); names libinza only in a zone C classification; treats segmental phonology only and says nothing about tone or pitch.

sources.citation: Sere, Sionvene K. K. 1985. Éléments de grammaire du Libinza: parler de Bolongo. Mémoire de licence, Université de Lubumbashi (UNILU).
